rationale: The implementation matches the ticket's prescribed scope exactly and the issuer key is verified end-to-end from YAML to the HTTP body, but two required acceptance criteria remain partial: AC7's gates (make ruff, make license-check, make test) were never executed - only two targeted pytest invocations are recorded (CR-001) - and AC6's definitive Claude Desktop check is out-of-repo and post-deploy, which the spec itself sequences after merge and the ConfigMap update. All four lenses ran with parseable output (verification-gap returned an empty set), the standards audit reported no coverage gap, the diff was not oversized, no decision_needed item remains, and 2.3 verified every candidate within budget. Nothing was deferred (0 defer, so no code-review-deferred.md was written) and 20 of 21 deduped candidates were dismissed after reading the source - the missing-import, test-auth-header and second-catalog-copy claims are false positives; the unvalidated-issuer-string family matches the zero validation on all six sibling fields and the declaration the ticket prescribes verbatim; the scalar-skips-entry and extra=ignore items are explicit non-goals or AC4 itself; the additive "authorizationServer": null key follows the payload's existing convention of serialising every absent optional field as null and cannot regress the 35 entries that are already broken; and the standards code-quality row is module-wide legacy typing style with the Ruff gate green. code-review-brief.md was written successfully.
risk_flags: additive nullable key on a public HTTP response consumed by external agent clients
the payload is served verbatim to those clients and must stay secret-free
per-entry validation is fail-closed, so a malformed value removes a whole server from the catalog
the definitive acceptance signal is out-of-repo and post-deploy

standards_review.notes: git-workflow.md Commit Message Format requires EPMCDME-####: Description (evidence README.md:163). Both subjects in the range match that form, each carrying the EPMCDME-14305 ticket prefix, a colon, a space and a capitalized sentence.

Met for most of what the guide covers: the Apache 2.0 header is present on the touched source file, 'from __future__ import annotations' is present, the loader keeps explicit parameter and return types, the Ruff line-length of 120 is respected (longest touched source line is 94 chars; the >120 lines in the touched test files are pre-existing and tests/* ignores E501 per pyproject.toml per-file-ignores), and first-party imports match the configured 'codemie' package. Unmet for the Types And Imports rule: the new field at src/codemie/configs/managed_mcp_config.py:81 is annotated Optional[List[str]], which is the form the guide's Avoid column names.

security-patterns.md is satisfied across everything this change touches. Secret Handling: the newly published field carries public IdP issuer URLs, ManagedMcpOAuthConfig declares no secret field, and extra=ignore keeps an unknown key such as clientSecret out of the API response; the example catalog uses example.com placeholders and states in-line that a client secret must never be placed there. Authentication: the /v1/mcp router still applies Depends(authenticate) to every route, so the widened payload is not newly exposed. Untrusted Input Handling: the loader uses yaml.safe_load, parses alias-only with populate_by_name deliberately unset, rejects a scalar authorizationServer instead of coercing it, and fails closed to an empty list rather than repairing malformed input. Observation not introduced by this change and unchanged from the base commit: the warning at src/codemie/configs/managed_mcp_config.py:154 logs the raw pre-validation entry dict, so a key dropped by extra=ignore would still reach log sinks.

findings.title: Required quality gates never executed
findings.problem: AC7 requires make ruff, make license-check and make test to pass, and all three targets exist (Makefile:30, :33, :48). The run record shows only two targeted pytest invocations over the two touched test files, so the lint gate, the license gate and the rest of the suite were never executed against this change.
findings.impact: A lint, license or unrelated-test regression would reach the merge queue unnoticed on a Blocker-priority fix. Static inspection puts the residual risk low - the added source line is 95 chars against a 120 limit, no import or dependency changed, and a repo-wide search confirms no test outside tests/codemie/rest_api/routers/test_mcp_managed.py pins the oauth payload shape that gained the seventh key - but the gates themselves remain unrun, so the acceptance criterion is unmet on evidence rather than on substance.
findings.recommendation: Run make ruff, make license-check and make test on this branch and record the results before merging; no code change is expected to be needed.
